board.synthesis: The 18 seeded perspectives agree on one physical obstacle lexicon, Founder fixed arenas, historical scars, a lean beach village, evidence-locked outcomes, and split world-technology/release gates. Dissent: the bigger the catalog, the more demanding the compatibility QA.

participants.title: The Closer
participants.assessment: One competition constitution, no sidecar canon; two summits must produce a source-linked executable change set.

participants.title: The Setup Man
participants.assessment: A modular 3-stage arena needs power, rigging, stage reset, broadcast failover, spectator routing and defined hazard states.

participants.title: The Scout
participants.assessment: Protect ESPN bracket, seeds and winners independently from all fictional competition forms and scene proposals.

participants.title: The Umpire
participants.assessment: Hard veto on invented historical fact, unapproved Atlas location writes, lethal principal-character mechanics, and unsourced claims.

participants.title: The Beat Writer
participants.assessment: Require opposing character strategies, active counters, escalation, one outcome, and emotional consequence; never a random gag montage.

participants.title: The Groundskeeper
participants.assessment: The old grounds need visible weathering, scar/repair/dormancy history and a maintenance schedule before every annual reuse.

participants.title: The GM
participants.assessment: Create a useful navigable obstacle lexicon and fixture-to-scene pipeline; measure adoption and distinctness, not list length alone.

participants.title: The Pitching Coach
participants.assessment: Constrained combinatorial challenge grammar and negative tests beat an open-ended thousands-of-prompts agent loop.

participants.title: The Warden
participants.assessment: Use restrained, survivable weaponry, projectile backstops, safe crowd barriers, water rescue and controlled pyrotechnics.

participants.title: The Commissioner
participants.assessment: Former champions and newcomers deserve neutral competition conditions; the bye is protected rest, not a fabricated victory.

participants.title: The Analyst
participants.assessment: A fictional points display cannot invent conversions from physical trial time to ESPN fantasy points; the real sports score remains locked.

participants.title: The Librarian
participants.assessment: Preserve 2015–25 team slots and venue dates; a 2025 screen may not appear in the 2015 original event.

participants.title: The Agent
participants.assessment: Make the audience understand each rule and tactical reversal in the first thirty seconds of a competition scene.

participants.title: The Bookkeeper
participants.assessment: Build reusable event rigs and maintenance budgets; no 120 unique stadiums, no magical no-cost modern broadcast expansion.

participants.title: The Commissioner General
participants.assessment: Honor the Michael Farrell memorial; use genre influences without copyrighted scene copying or invented biographies.

participants.title: The Clubhouse Manager
participants.assessment: Assign actual support roles—stewards, referees, operators, registrars, stage builders—across changing era capacities.

participants.title: The Scout Master
participants.assessment: Spectator logistics, premium suites, resort accessibility and a dignified championship procession must reinforce, not overwhelm, competition.

participants.title: The Architect
participants.assessment: Implement round-fixed venue capabilities and an Atlas-derived spatial compatibility contract; do not fork World OS.

consultants.name: Jeff Lunsford
consultants.disclaimer: Research-based analytical lens; not a live consultation with Jeff Lunsford.
consultants.review: The opportunity is a reusable production product: one lexicon feeding interactive Atlas preview, weekly Memo and historical Novel. Overbuilding 120 bespoke rigs is poor leverage. Measure stories rendered per certified venue capability and do not promote a raw catalog without readers comprehending it.

consultants.name: John Ezzell
consultants.disclaimer: Research-based analytical lens; not a live consultation with John Ezzell.
consultants.review: Treat challenge registry as candidate content, not geography truth. Stable IDs, source-of-truth boundaries, schema versioning, interoperability contracts and negative tests prevent two competing Atlas maps. Reusing the exact venue IDs in the current PR is essential.

consultants.name: Tim Veil
consultants.disclaimer: Research-based analytical lens; not a live consultation with Tim Veil.
consultants.review: The system must be reproducible and fail closed: frozen historical result spine, seeded or deterministic challenge selection, valid site affordances, explicit era state, no unverified 2026 fixtures, and independent quality gates. Model or simulator output never authorizes canon.
